title: Declarative agents: what Copilot runs for you, what it needs and where to stop it
summary: Hold: the block API operates on a Copilot package, but the table promises that it affects only the agent and not its package. The page also sends readers to Tools for connected-service permissions and credentials, and understates the security controls available through agent management rules.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Blocking acts on the agent only
claims.claim: The agent actions page says selected-agent actions do not necessarily apply to its whole plugin package or bundled capabilities.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections.
claims.fix: Keep the cited page's qualification, but rename this bullet 'Agent and package boundaries' and add: 'The plugin governance page separately says a package containing an agent and a skill appears under Tools and Agents as one entity; those views do not make its capabilities independently governed packages.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/manage#understand-package-and-skill-blocking.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Blocking acts on the agent only

claims.where: Risks and limits: Blocking acts on the agent only
claims.claim: The instruction 'Manage those under Agents > Tools' includes the connected-service permissions, credentials and connections just named.
claims.quote: Connection or account | The product that owns authentication and the connection | Manage sign-in, authorization, source permissions, connection scope, and revocation separately.
claims.fix: Replace 'Manage those under Agents > Tools' with 'Manage plugins, skills and MCP servers under Agents > Tools; manage connected-service permissions, credentials and connections separately in the product that owns them.' The first clause is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions and the second at https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/manage#apply-a-component-control-when-required.
